benchmark_metadata.title: Phase 4 Cybersecurity Claim Verification Benchmark
benchmark_metadata.description: Reproducible benchmark dataset for evaluating claim-level evidence verification, epistemic segregation, and hallucination reduction across multimodal cybersecurity evidence.

test_cases.description: Claim directly supported by Windows EVTX and Mordor telemetry.

claim.text: LSASS memory read access was detected targeting the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service, consistent with credential dumping (T1003).

test_cases.description: Claim supported by visual terminal screenshot OCR and MITRE ATT&CK.
test_cases.query: Show terminal capture or screenshot of Mimikatz execution

claim.text: Visual terminal capture shows interactive Mimikatz executing privilege::debug and sekurlsa::logonpasswords commands (T1003.001).

test_cases.description: PowerShell execution bypass is verified, but unobserved cloud exfiltration is extrapolated.
test_cases.query: What evidence is associated with PowerShell execution and bypass?

claim.text: PowerShell was spawned with -ExecutionPolicy Bypass (T1059.001) and exfiltrated sensitive corporate documents to an external Amazon S3 bucket.

test_cases.description: Claim asserts browser password theft with zero supporting evidence.

claim.text: The adversary extracted stored passwords and session tokens from Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox browser SQLite databases.

test_cases.description: Claim asserts Linux/Bash execution, contradicting Windows PowerShell telemetry.
test_cases.query: What evidence is associated with PowerShell execution?

claim.text: The entire incident execution was conducted on an Ubuntu Linux server via Bash scripts without any Windows systems involved.

test_cases.description: Claim asserts APT29 attribution when evidence contains only generic vulnerability details.

claim.text: The Log4Shell CVE-2021-44228 vulnerability exploitation was definitively attributed to Russian intelligence state-sponsored group APT29 (Cozy Bear).
